newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly up on wheat gains, options.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly up on wheat gains, options.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended mostly higher on Friday, boosted by sharp gains in wheat and by bullishly-construed options plays, traders said.

Wheat futures remained volatile amid conflicting signals about the extent of freeze damage that occurred last weekend in key U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat areas, traders said. Damage estimates varied widely from 50 million bushels to 200 million.
Corn was also supported by active options buying, most notably in the July calls. The May options expired on Friday which added to buying interest in the July, pit sources said.

Traders said Lind-Waldock bought at least 1,200 July $3.20 calls at seven to 7-1/4 cents. Cargill Investor Services bought 100 July $3.30 calls at 4-3/4 cents and FCC bought 200 July $3.30 calls at 4-1/2 cents.
Corn futures ended 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 1/4 cent lower with May up 3-1/4 at $3.00-1/4 a bushel.

New crop months were weakened by reports some U.S Midwest farmers expected to plant corn this weekend despite cool weather. Some floor sources also pointed to ideas corn acreage would increase if a U.S. House subcommittee plan to limit CRP enrollment to 14 million acres passed.

The 14 million acres were far smaller than the 19 million acres mentioned in USDA documents. A USDA spokesman said it was too early to set a cap on CRP and the American Farm Bureau Federation said the cap was unfair and unwise.
If the cap were passed, traders said it could release additional acreage for corn plantings.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought five million bushels December, bringing their weekly corn purchase tally near 25 million bushels, pit sources said.
Traders said Refco Inc bought 4.5 million bushels July but sold 1.5 million July while Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought one million each May and July.

ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp spread at least four million bushels May/July at 3/4 cents, premium July, and Prudential Securities and R.J. O'Brien each spread 1.5 million bushles July/May at 1/2 to one cent, premium July, traders said.
The July/December spread closed at 16-3/4 cents, premium July, up 1-3/4 from Thursday.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 66,000 contracts, below Thursday's actual volume of 74,889.
Options volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, against Thursday's actual of 16,936 lots.
